111:python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG --migration-batches COORD
114:`--migration-batches` exposes the one fixed migration-batch coordination ledger at `COORD` as read-only `GET /migration-batches` and its incremental change stream at `GET /migration-batches/events`; it may only be given together with `--audit` and the multi-token `--auth` method — alone, empty, repeated, without `--audit` or paired with the single `--token` it is a usage error (exit status 2) and nothing listens. The client can neither pass nor probe any other file path: the ledger is fixed at startup. Without it both paths stay a plain 404 like any other unknown path, and every other interface is unchanged.
116:Authorization is the existing audit authorization and the request order is fixed — identity, query parameters, scope, and only then the ledger read; a failure at one stage never opens a later stage's files. A missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` gets 401 `unauthorized`, an unknown or expired token 403 `forbidden`, and an unreadable or invalid configuration 503 `auth_unavailable`. Unknown, repeated or empty parameters and illegal combinations get 400 `invalid_request`. `GET /migration-batches?key=K` returns only that batch's snapshot; the key stands alone, so `cursor` or `limit` beside it is 400, and an unknown batch is a distinct 404 `migration_batch_not_found`. Without `key` the query paginates in ascending batch-key code-point order with an exclusive `cursor` and a `limit` page size (a decimal integer from 1 to 1000, default 100). The page object has, in order, `entries` and `next`; each entry carries, in order, the batch `key`, the complete batch `snapshot` and `completion`. An active batch's `completion` is `null`; a terminal batch's completion is `{"index": i, "at": t}` — the batch's zero-based position in the coordination audit (the real completion order) and its completion moment — so the public completion order and per-item errors are observable. `next` is the key of the page's last entry when more batches remain, else `null`.
118:`GET /migration-batches/events` resumes the incremental progress stream by persisted position: every durable coordination commit that changes an observable batch appends one event, covering batch creation, an ownership takeover after the coordination lease expires, an item's phase transition or saved error, a step receipt landing in the item snapshot, and batch closure. Equivalent replays, coordination-lease renewals and waits on an unchanged plan append nothing. The query takes only an exclusive decimal non-negative-integer `cursor` (omit it to read from position 0; only strictly greater positions are considered), the same 1-to-1000 decimal `limit` (default 100) and optional non-empty string filters `key` (batch key) and `job` (related job id), combined by logical AND; filtered positions never consume page capacity. The page object has, in order, `events` and `next`; each event carries, in fixed order, its strictly increasing zero-based `position` (never reused), the commit moment `at`, the batch `key`, the related `job_id` (`null` for batch-scoped changes), the `category` (`created`, `taken_over`, `item`, `receipt`, `completed`) and the complete post-commit batch `snapshot`. `next` is the page's last position when more matching events remain (it need not match anything itself), else `null`. Unknown or repeated parameters, empty values, a non-decimal `cursor` or an out-of-range `limit` get 400 `invalid_request`. A coordination ledger written before the stream existed keeps loading read-only byte-for-byte and simply yields no events; the first later write upgrades it and seeds one `completed` event per existing audit entry in audit order before appending that run's own events.
122:The coordination ledger's shared lock together with the nine business ledgers' shared locks covers the ledger reads, the page/snapshot/event formation and the response serialization, so a concurrent batch writer is observed as either the complete old or the complete new version, never a mix; responses are compact UTF-8 JSON with no trailing newline. Before any lock or business ledger is touched, an existing coordination file must first prove its own format — UTF-8, JSON (no negative-zero or non-finite literals), version 1, the fixed field sets and key order and the exact canonical bytes; any such violation raises even when the requested key is absent and is never masked by it. The read never creates the coordination file, a lock file, a directory or any other trace: a miss is decided by an unlocked read before a companion lock file is opened. A missing coordination ledger gets 404 `migration_batches_not_found`; non-canonical content, a broken cross-reference or a referenced business ledger that is missing gets 409 `migration_batches_invalid`; any other read failure gets 503 `migration_batches_unavailable`. Error bodies contain only `error` and never leak a path or system message.
124:The library surface is `migration_batch.get(ledger, key)` (one snapshot, `KeyError` for a missing ledger or unknown key), `migration_batch.search(ledger, cursor=None, limit=100)` (the page object), `migration_batch.events(ledger, cursor=None, limit=100, *, key=None, job_id=None)` (one page of the incremental stream) and the lock-holding `get_response`/`search_response`/`events_response` serializers the endpoint serves. For the plain event query the coordination ledger's shared lock together with the nine business ledgers' shared locks covers the argument validation, the filtering, the pagination and the response serialization (the non-HTTP `events` builder forms its page under the same lock group), so a concurrent writer is observed as one complete version. The on-disk ledger gains an optional fourth section, the append-only `events` list in the fixed order `version`, `batches`, `audit`, `events`: baseline ledgers with just the first three sections stay valid and replay byte-for-byte under read-only callers, and the first subsequent write appends the section (seeding it from the audit) in the same atomic commit as any other change.
129:python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG --migration-batches COORD --migration-consumers CONSUMERS
132:`--migration-consumers` adds the persistent-consumer layer on top of the position-resuming event stream: durable consumer cursors, owner leases, acknowledgements and dead letters kept in one consumer ledger at `CONSUMERS`, independent of the coordination ledger it reads. It only enables together with `--migration-batches` (and therefore `--audit` and the multi-token `--auth` method) — alone, empty, repeated, without `--migration-batches`, without `--audit` or paired with the single `--token` it is a usage error (exit status 2) and nothing listens. Once configured it opens four write endpoints (`claim`, `pull`, `ack`, `reject`) and two read-only endpoints (`status`, `dead-letters`); the client never names a coordination or consumer ledger path (both are fixed at startup) and every body is one JSON object with a fixed field set. Without the option all six paths stay a plain 404 like any unknown path, and every other interface is unchanged.
134:`POST /migration-consumers/claim` claims or renews one named consumer. Its body is exactly `consumer`, `owner`, `now` (a non-boolean non-negative integer moment), `lease` (a non-boolean positive integer window), `idem` (the non-empty idempotency key) and the optional non-empty-string filters `key` (one fixed batch key) and `job_id` (one related job id); both filters may be omitted or carried as JSON `null`, and no other field is accepted. The first claim persists the subscription, the owner, the lease end (`now + lease`) and the initial `null` acknowledged position, and answers the claim object in fixed order: `consumer`, `key`, `job_id`, `owner`, `until`, `position`, `taken_over`. The subscription is immutable: a later claim carrying another `key` or `job_id` is 400 `invalid_request`, and a claim without `key` stays a permanent cross-batch range. A repeat claim by the same owner under a new `idem` extends the lease only while the lease is still valid — a claim moment equal to `until` still renews, but once the lease has strictly expired even that owner may no longer renew in place: the claim answers 409 `migration_consumer_ownership` and leaves the ledger byte-for-byte untouched. Another owner is refused with 409 `migration_consumer_ownership` while the lease is valid (the lease is valid through `until`, so a claim at exactly `until` is still refused) and may take over only once it has strictly expired — the answer then carries `taken_over: true`, the owner and `until` change and the acknowledged position is preserved, so unacknowledged events redeliver.
136:`POST /migration-consumers/pull` returns the events after the acknowledged position. Its body is exactly `consumer`, `owner`, `now` and an optional 1..1000 `limit` (default 100); it takes no idempotency key. The answer carries, in order, `consumer`, `owner`, `until`, `position`, `events` and `next`; `events` and `next` reuse the event stream's fixed event shape, ordering, page size and continuation semantics, filtered by the consumer's fixed subscription (the batch key and job filter combine by logical AND and filtered positions never consume page capacity). A pull never advances the checkpoint and never writes, and a rejected event is never returned (it stays observable through the dead-letter query below). `POST /migration-consumers/ack` moves it forward: its body is exactly `consumer`, `owner`, `now`, `position` and `idem`. The answer carries `consumer`, `owner`, `until`, `position`. Acknowledgement may only move forward to the position of a real event the fixed subscription matches in the current stream. An ack equal to the current position changes and writes nothing and answers 200 (the equivalent `idem` replay returns the original answer); a backward ack or one past the stream tail is 400 `invalid_request`; a position the stream has truncated, rewritten or reused behind the cursor is 409 `migration_consumer_checkpoint` and the cursor is never reset automatically.

"""Persistent consumers of the migration-batch progress stream.

The ``migration_batch`` coordination ledger publishes one append-only
incremental event stream; this module owns the durable consumer side
of that stream. A persistent consumer keeps its own independent
ledger, bound forever to one resolved coordination ledger path: a
claim fixes the subscription -- one optional fixed batch key and one
optional job filter -- the owner, the lease end and the acknowledged
stream position; a pull returns the matching events after that
position without advancing it, and an ack moves the position forward
to a real matching event. A repeat claim by the live owner extends
the lease only while it is still valid (the moment equal to the lease
end counts); once it has strictly expired even the former owner may
not renew in place and gets TimeoutError with the ledger untouched,
while a different owner may take over. Only the current owner while
the lease is valid may pull or ack; after strict expiry another owner
may take over without changing the position, so unacknowledged events
redeliver.

A reject (the fourth consume operation) is an ack that also dead-
letters the event: only the current owner during a valid lease may
reject, and the position must name the earliest unacknowledged event
the fixed subscription still matches -- predecessors may not be
skipped and the stream tail may not be passed. The cursor advances to
that position in the same atomic commit that records the dead letter,

through the dead-letter query (:func:`consumer_dead_letters`). A
